key_insight: SAP-ViT replaces CLS-token classification with patch-embedding aggregation, making predictions decomposable into patch-level contributions.
clinical_relevance: Patch-level explanations could help researchers inspect image evidence behind medical image classifications, but clinical utility is not established.
method: Aggregate final-layer patch embeddings directly for classification.
Apply sparsity regularization to encourage concise patch-level evidence.
Estimate input-patch contributions through back-mapping that accounts for attention mixing.
evidence_signal: Across multiple medical imaging datasets and modalities, the abstract reports strong classification performance and interpretable explanations, with ablations supporting sparsity regularization and back-mapping alignment.
watch_item: Back-mapping estimates input contributions; the abstract provides no numerical results or clinical validation.
paper_title: SAP-ViT: A Self-Attributing Patch Vision Transformer for Medical Image Classification
